objectives.en: Define a stack and the LIFO principle
List applications of stacks in computing

narration.en: In the canteen you always take the plate from the top of the pile, the one that was placed last. Computers use the same idea for undo, the back button and more.
narration.kn: ಕ್ಯಾಂಟೀನ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ತಟ್ಟೆಗಳ ರಾಶಿಯ ಮೇಲಿನ ತಟ್ಟೆಯನ್ನೇ ತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ, ಅದು ಕೊನೆಗೆ ಇಟ್ಟದ್ದು. ಕಂಪ್ಯೂಟರ್ undo, back ಬಟನ್‌ಗಳಿಗೆ ಇದೇ ತತ್ವ ಬಳಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: A data structure defines how data is organised so that it can be used efficiently. A stack is a linear data structure in which elements are added and removed at only one end, called the TOP. The element added last is removed first, so a stack follows the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle.

points.en: Examples: pile of plates, books, clothes, bangles on the wrist

narration.en: A data structure defines how data is organised so that it can be used efficiently. A stack is a linear data structure in which elements are added and removed at only one end, called the TOP. The element added last is removed first, so a stack follows the Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) principle.
narration.kn: ಸ್ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ ಒಂದು ರೇಖೀಯ ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ರಚನೆ. ಇದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರಿಸುವುದು ಮತ್ತು ತೆಗೆಯುವುದು TOP ಎಂಬ ಒಂದೇ ತುದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇದು LIFO ತತ್ವ ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: A stack of plates: Last In, First Out

say.en: A stack is like a pile of plates. We can add or remove a plate only at the top.
The end where we add and remove is called the TOP. Here the TOP is P3.
PUSH adds P4 on top. POP removes the top element, which is the last one added: Last In, First Out.
Programs use stacks whenever the newest item must be handled first.

narration.en: We draw a stack growing upward, mark its TOP, and list where programs use stacks.

prompt.en: Match each application with how the stack is used in it.
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಅನ್ವಯವನ್ನು ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ ಬಳಕೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೊಂದಿಸಿ.

right.en: Each change is pushed; undo pops the most recent change
Each page visited is pushed; back pops to the last page
Push every character, then pop them all
Push each ( and pop one at every )
Operators wait on the stack until their turn
Operands are pushed; each operator pops two and pushes the result
The plate placed last is the first one taken

explanation.en: All of these need the most recent item first, which is exactly Last-In-First-Out: push and pop happen only at the TOP.
explanation.kn: ಇವೆಲ್ಲಕ್ಕೂ ಇತ್ತೀಚಿನದು ಮೊದಲು ಬೇಕು: ಇದೇ LIFO; push, pop TOP ನಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ.

body.en: Programs use a stack whenever the most recent item must be handled first: reversing a string, undo and redo in text and image editors, the back button of a web browser, checking that parentheses in an expression are matched, and converting and evaluating arithmetic expressions.

narration.en: Programs use a stack whenever the most recent item must be handled first: reversing a string, undo and redo in text and image editors, the back button of a web browser, checking that parentheses in an expression are matched, and converting and evaluating arithmetic expressions.
narration.kn: ಇತ್ತೀಚಿನ ಅಂಶವನ್ನು ಮೊದಲು ನಿರ್ವಹಿಸಬೇಕಾದಾಗ ಸ್ಟ್ಯಾಕ್ ಬಳಸುತ್ತಾರೆ: ಸ್ಟ್ರಿಂಗ್ ತಿರುಗಿಸುವುದು, undo/redo, ಬ್ರೌಸರ್ back ಬಟನ್, ಆವರಣ ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ, ಅಭಿವ್ಯಕ್ತಿ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ.

caption.en: Push plates onto a stack and pop them off: the last one in is the first one out.

Pop until empty, then pop again.

narration.en: Push every letter, then pop them all. The last letter pushed comes out first.
Class quiz. Discuss, raise hands, and the monitor taps the class answer.
narration.kn: ತರಗತಿ ರಸಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ. ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ, ಕೈ ಎತ್ತಿ, ಮಾನಿಟರ್ ತರಗತಿಯ ಉತ್ತರವನ್ನು ಒತ್ತಲಿ.

points.en: A stack is a linear data structure with one open end, the TOP.
